---
title: Themes
description: A theme is a set of tokens. Switch the look with one attribute.
---
import ThemeSwitch from '../../../components/ThemeSwitch.astro';

A theme gives every colour token a value, for light and, if it has one, for dark. The measures (radii, spacing,
motion) stay the same in every theme. Switching is one attribute, on the whole page or on one box:

<ThemeSwitch />

`herefront` is light only — it stays light even when the page asks for dark, as the client cabinet does.

## Make your own theme

1. Copy `tokens/themes/dashboard.json` to `tokens/themes/<name>.json` and change the values. Every key of `dashboard`
   must be there (a test checks it), so no component ever meets an empty colour.
2. Set `"$scheme"` to `auto` (light and dark), `light` or `dark`.
3. `npm run build` — the theme is now `data-hf-theme="<name>"`.

## Customising, from the most common to the rarest

1. **Tokens and themes** — a different palette, radii, density, glass.
2. **Attributes** — a variant or a state: `variant`, `size`, `tone`, `disabled`.
3. **`::part()`** — one part inside a component, from a stable, documented list.
4. **Slots** — your own content: an icon, a label, a trailing value.
5. **A component's own variable** (`--hf-button-h`) — for one place, without a new theme.

Never `!important` and never the internal classes: if 1–5 cannot do it, it belongs in herefront-ui.
